text:
jerry: Heads-up — after the 1.29 roll to us-east-prod we're seeing the cluster-autoscaler not scale GPU nodegroups at all. Pods stay Pending with GPU requests. Anyone seen this pattern?

maria: yep saw it ~10:30. kube-controller logs show CA ignoring nodegroup annotations on the ASG nodes. quick log: 
```
I0318 10:31:12.123456 1 utils.go:210] couldn't map node to nodeGroup: missing annotation 'nodegroup.redwood.com/id'
I0318 10:31:12.123457 1 scale_up.go:345] no candidate nodeGroups for pending pods
```

alex: I reproduced on staging earlier. Looks like k8s 1.29 changed how cloudprovider exposes NodeGroupRef -> CA expected annotation key `nodegroup.redwood.com/id` but the cloud-controller-manager now emits `nodepool.redwood.com/id`. CA fails to fall back.

sasha: Confirmed with `kubectl get nodes -o jsonpath='{.items[*].metadata.annotations}' | grep nodepool` — nodes have `nodepool.redwood.com/id` only. Our CA version (v1.22-custom) only checks the old key.

infra-bot: deploy-event: canary/ca-v1.22-custom rolled to us-east-stage at 2025-11-09T10:15:00Z

jerry: Could we either patch CA to check both keys or add the legacy annotation as a temporary migration? Which is faster?

maria: patching CA is safer but takes time for canary/rollout. Quick mitigation: one-off job that copies nodepool.* -> nodegroup.* on nodes so autoscaler sees them. Small script: 
```
for n in $(kubectl get nodes -l 'alpha.kubernetes.io/instance-type'=p4 -o name); do
  id=$(kubectl get $n -o jsonpath='{.metadata.annotations["nodepool.redwood.com/id"]}')
  kubectl annotate $n nodegroup.redwood.com/id="${id}" --overwrite
done
```
This will let CA consider the GPU nodegroups immediately.

alex: I'll open a CA patch to add a fallback check for `nodepool.redwood.com/id` and include unit tests. PR: https://github.com/redwood/cluster-autoscaler/pull/827 (draft) — it tries both keys before failing.

sasha: For production I'm +1 for the CA change. We'll need to ship it through our infra-images and do a canary rollout. In the meantime I can run maria's annotator as a CronJob in us-east-prod for a few hours.

deploy-bot: canary-deploy request: cluster-autoscaler:redwood/ca:v1.22-hotfix -> us-east-canary queued

maria: FYI cluster-ops cost note — annotating nodes won't change costs but if CA stays offline we may hit capacity shortages and push expensive on-demand GPUs. Keep an eye on queued GPU pods.

alex: PR opened and linked tests. Two-line change + comment referencing k8s 1.29 behaviour. cc @jerry @sasha — will request review from infra and runtime.

sasha: I applied the annotator cronjob to us-east-prod canary (runs every 5m). First run added ~42 nodegroup annotations, CA immediately registered them and scheduled scale-ups for pending GPU pods.

jerry: Nice. Can we make the annotator self-limiting (run for 12h) and then delete if CA rollout succeeds?

maria: done — cronjob spec had `completions: 0` and a TTL controller to clear after 12h. K8s job finished and deleted automatically.

infra-bot: pr-merge: https://github.com/redwood/cluster-autoscaler/pull/827 merged by alex (main) at 2025-11-09T13:02:43Z

deploy-bot: rollout: cluster-autoscaler:v1.22-hotfix -> us-east-canary succeeded.

sasha: Hotfix image built, promoted to canary and then to us-east-prod. Observability shows scale events resumed within ~4 minutes after pod restart.

jerry: Confirmed — all pending GPU pods in us-east-prod are now scheduling, node count increased to meet demand and latency for critical jobs back to normal.

maria: Follow-up action items: 1) add e2e to infra-tests to validate both `nodegroup.*` and `nodepool.*` annotation handling; 2) update our k8s upgrade playbook to include annotation compatibility checks; 3) add telemetry alert if CA reports `no candidate nodeGroups` for >5m.

alex: I'll add the e2e and the alert rule (Prometheus).

sasha: Closing thread once alerts created and playbook updated. Thanks all for the quick turnaround :thumbsup:

jerry: Great work. Leaving a short postmortem note in incidents later.
